Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- Tickets REQ-2400–2409: large east-region requests (shipment, claim, invoice, refund) need assignment to the right desk.
- Tried option C (“regional office” / “region”) on all 10. Every outcome: Rejected, +0.00. Conclusion: C is invalid for this request class. Do not choose C again.
- Sender/team, subject wording, and urgency cues (“no rush”, “client asking twice”, “second attempt”, “before end of day”, “confirm receipt”) did not make C valid. They are not reliable routing criteria.
- Remaining plausible options: A (standard queue), B (priority desk), and possibly D if shown. Next, test A or B.
- Leading hypothesis: B (priority desk), because requests are described as “large” and all originate from the east region. No positive evidence yet.
- If B is rejected, test A. Keep tracking outcomes to confirm the correct desk and whether request type changes routing.
- Avoid repeating failed C attempts; seek a successful outcome before generalizing further.

- Option B (priority desk): tested on REQ-2410–2419. Accepted (+1.00) for invoice and shipment. Rejected (+0.00) for all refunds: 2411, 2413, 2414, 2418.

- Current rule: large east-region invoice -> B. Large east-region shipment -> B.
- Current hypothesis: large east-region refund -> A (standard queue). B and C failed for refunds; A is the remaining likely option. Test A on next refund.
- If A fails for refund, test D if shown. Keep tracking refund outcomes and any claim cases; do not assume claims follow invoice/shipment or refund without evidence.
- Avoid repeating failed C. Avoid B for refunds unless new evidence contradicts.
